chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Jamil ibn Salih, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, who said: I asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) about Mut'ah (temporary marriage), and he said: 'It is permissible for you by Allah and His Messenger.' I said: 'What is its limit/duration?' He said: 'Among its limits is that you do not inherit her, nor does she inherit you.' I said: 'Then what is her waiting period (Iddah)?' He said: 'Fifty-five days or one complete menstrual cycle.'
ai.seo_question: What is the duration and inheritance rule for temporary marriage (Mut'ah) in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes Mut'ah as a distinct marital contract with specific legal boundaries, notably excluding mutual inheritance rights. The specification of the Iddah as either forty-five days or one complete menstrual cycle highlights the jurisprudential nuance in determining the waiting period for temporary spouses, distinguishing it from permanent marriage.
